text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Police question Netanyahu
- U.S. criticises Jerusalem road construction
- Lebanese police nab Okamoto, 6 others
- First internet auction: Memorabilia from Dreyfus affair
- Shabak head Ayalon hedges on Har Homa
- Peace Now vows to block Har Homa
- IDF, SLA on alert for Hizbollah retaliation
HAARETZ
- Minister Eitan asks lawyers to check whether Tzomet can quit agreement with Likud
- Army reexamining idea of appointing internal comptroller
- Treasury forms special committee against black capital
- City of Jerusalem seeks land for Orthodox equivalent of Yad Vashem holocaust memorial
- Average income in Savion three times higher than Kiryat Shmona
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu cooperated with police, answered all questions; Danny Naveh also testified yesterday
- Mordechai's helicopter emergency-landed after dropping him off and taking off again.
- Knesset member says 3 died over 15 years in accidents in Biological institute
MAARIV
- Deri lawyer Avi-Yitzhak resigns
- Fear in northern settlements of Hizbollah rockets
- Tel Aviv Stock Exchange continues soaring
- Shabak, police warn building Har Homa can ignite riots
- New settlement being built in West Bank, 50 houses completed
